title: Get started
text: {strainselect} helps choosing bacterial strains sequence collection described metadata (sampling context, matrix, region, sector, year…). offers two complementary methods: clustering method (assess_gower(), cstats_table(), select_silhouette()) suited number strains can sequenced limited. Strains grouped k clusters similar strains best clustered strain cluster selected, selected strains different possible ; profile method (prepare_upset(), define_profiles(), select_profiles()) suited number strains sequence limited. Strains sharing exactly metadata grouped one strain per group selected, every distinct profile — including unique strains — represented. methods start prepare_input(), cleans raw table. examples use data_test.csv, table 100 Salmonella strains described 24 variables, shipped package. selection based 6 variables: CONTEXTE, MATRICE1, REGION, SECTEUR, LIEUPVT year extracted DATE_PRELEVEMENT.

title: Get started
text: using methods, dataset must cleaned contain metadata selection based. prepare_input(): checks strain identifiers unique (stops list duplicated identifiers otherwise); uses identifiers row names; keeps selected metadata columns; optionally extracts year (ANNEE) /month (MOIS) date column; replaces missing values "unknown" converts every column factor. Columns can given names (recommended, easier read depend order columns) positions. Dates read date_format, "%d/%m/%Y" (e.g. 09/01/2020) default; use instance date_format = "%Y-%m-%d" dates 2020-01-09. date column already class Date used .
code: datafile <- system.file("data_test.csv", package = "strainselect") raw_data <- read.csv(datafile, sep = ";", header = TRUE) prepared_data <- prepare_input(   raw_data,   col_select = c("CONTEXTE", "MATRICE1", "REGION", "SECTEUR", "LIEUPVT"),   id = "IDENTIFIANT", date = "DATE_PRELEVEMENT", month = FALSE, year = TRUE ) #> no duplicate ID #> selected metadata: CONTEXTE, MATRICE1, REGION, SECTEUR, LIEUPVT, ANNEE head(prepared_data) #>                   CONTEXTE         MATRICE1               REGION #> 2020LSAL00151 Surveillance     non spécifié Auvergne Rhone Alpes #> 2020LSAL00152 Surveillance     non spécifié Auvergne Rhone Alpes #> 2020LSAL00163 Surveillance Viande de canard   Nouvelle Aquitaine #> 2020LSAL00167 Surveillance Viande de canard            Occitanie #> 2020LSAL00176 Surveillance    Gallus gallus   Nouvelle Aquitaine #> 2020LSAL00177 Surveillance           Dindes             Bretagne #>                                    SECTEUR #> 2020LSAL00151                  Eco-système #> 2020LSAL00152                  Eco-système #> 2020LSAL00163         Alimentation humaine #> 2020LSAL00167         Alimentation humaine #> 2020LSAL00176 Santé et production animales #> 2020LSAL00177 Santé et production animales #>                                                     LIEUPVT ANNEE #> 2020LSAL00151                       Source/captage de l'eau  2020 #> 2020LSAL00152                       Source/captage de l'eau  2020 #> 2020LSAL00163                   Transformation industrielle  2020 #> 2020LSAL00167                   Transformation industrielle  2020 #> 2020LSAL00176 Lieu d'exploitation, d'élevage, ou de culture  2020 #> 2020LSAL00177 Lieu d'exploitation, d'élevage, ou de culture  2020 # the same with column positions prepared_data <- prepare_input(raw_data, col_select = c(7, 10, 13, 14, 17, 24),                                id = 1, date = 17) #> no duplicate ID #> selected metadata: CONTEXTE, MATRICE1, REGION, SECTEUR, LIEUPVT, ANNEE

title: Get started
text: clustering method uses three functions: assess_gower(), cstats_table() select_silhouette(). cstats_table() optional number strains sequence fixed advance.

title: Get started
text: assess_gower() computes dissimilarity matrix strains using Gower distance, suited categorical metadata. Weights can given metadata adjust importance clustering. hierarchical clustering complete linkage performed matrix, dendrogram drawn graph = TRUE.
code: datafile <- system.file("data_test.csv", package = "strainselect") raw_data <- read.csv(datafile, sep = ";", header = TRUE) prepared_data <- prepare_input(raw_data, col_select = c(7, 10, 13, 14, 17, 24),                                id = 1, date = 17) #> no duplicate ID #> selected metadata: CONTEXTE, MATRICE1, REGION, SECTEUR, LIEUPVT, ANNEE gower <- assess_gower(prepared_data, graph = TRUE)

what: Choosing the number of clusters: cstats_table
title: Get started
text: cstats_table() computes clustering statistics (see fpc::cluster.stats()) increasing number clusters: step, 2 * step, …, k. average silhouette width (avg.silwidth) useful one: plotted number clusters, optimal number clusters marked maximum plateau curve. idea test large number clusters without exceeding number strains can sequenced; larger step reduces computing time.
code: datafile <- system.file("data_test.csv", package = "strainselect") raw_data <- read.csv(datafile, sep = ";", header = TRUE) prepared_data <- prepare_input(raw_data, col_select = c(7, 10, 13, 14, 17, 24),                                id = 1, date = 17) #> no duplicate ID #> selected metadata: CONTEXTE, MATRICE1, REGION, SECTEUR, LIEUPVT, ANNEE gower <- assess_gower(prepared_data, graph = FALSE) stats <- cstats_table(dist = gower$gower_dist, tree = gower$aggl.clust.c,                       k = 50, step = 10) #> testing 10 clusters #> testing 20 clusters #> testing 30 clusters #> testing 40 clusters #> testing 50 clusters stats[, c("cluster.number", "avg.silwidth")] #>         cluster.number avg.silwidth #> Test 10             10         0.29 #> Test 20             20         0.41 #> Test 30             30         0.39 #> Test 40             40         0.49 #> Test 50             50         0.48

title: Get started
text: last step selects one strain sequence cluster. number clusters k either chosen silhouette plot set number strains can sequenced. cluster, strain largest silhouette width — .e. best clustered strain — selected. several strains share largest silhouette width cluster, one chosen random; use seed make choice reproducible.
code: datafile <- system.file("data_test.csv", package = "strainselect") raw_data <- read.csv(datafile, sep = ";", header = TRUE) prepared_data <- prepare_input(raw_data, col_select = c(7, 10, 13, 14, 17, 24),                                id = 1, date = 17) #> no duplicate ID #> selected metadata: CONTEXTE, MATRICE1, REGION, SECTEUR, LIEUPVT, ANNEE gower <- assess_gower(prepared_data, graph = FALSE) selection <- select_silhouette(prepared_data, dist = gower$gower_dist, k = 20,                                seed = 1) # the 20 strains to sequence unique(selection$selected) #>  [1] "2020LSAL00802" "2020LSAL00487" "2020LSAL00177" "2020LSAL00854" #>  [5] "2020LSAL00454" "2020LSAL00720" "2020LSAL00506" "2020LSAL00550" #>  [9] "2020LSAL00660" "2020LSAL00668" "2020LSAL00724" "2020LSAL00790" #> [13] "2020LSAL00912" "2020LSAL00792" "2020LSAL00866" "2020LSAL00892" #> [17] "2020LSAL01016" "2020LSAL00994" "2020LSAL01040" "2020LSAL01188"

title: Get started
text: method groups strains strictly identical selected metadata, selects one strain per group. Unlike clustering method, strains group identical, strains similar strain form group . uses three functions: prepare_upset(), define_profiles() select_profiles().

title: Get started
text: prepare_upset() creates binary table prepared data: one column per modality metadata (named <metadata> _ <modality>), filled 1 strain modality 0 otherwise. binary table can used visualise groups identical strains UpSet plot, instance {UpSetR} package:

the 12 most frequent modalities UpSetR::upset(upset_data, nsets = 12, order.by = "freq", nintersects = 20,               mb.ratio = c(0.55, 0.45), text.scale = 1.1) #> Warning: `aes_string()` was deprecated in ggplot2 3.0.0. #> ℹ Please use tidy evaluation idioms with `aes()`. #> ℹ See also `vignette("ggplot2-in-packages")` for more information. #> ℹ The deprecated feature was likely used in the UpSetR package. #>   Please report the issue at <https://github.com/hms-dbmi/UpSetR/issues>. #> This warning is displayed once per session. #> Call `lifecycle::last_lifecycle_warnings()` to see where this warning was #> generated. #> Warning: Using `size` aesthetic for lines was deprecated in ggplot2 3.4.0. #> ℹ Please use `linewidth` instead. #> ℹ The deprecated feature was likely used in the UpSetR package. #>   Please report the issue at <https://github.com/hms-dbmi/UpSetR/issues>. #> This warning is displayed once per session. #> Call `lifecycle::last_lifecycle_warnings()` to see where this warning was #> generated. #> Warning: The `size` argument of `element_line()` is deprecated as of ggplot2 3.4.0. #> ℹ Please use the `linewidth` argument instead. #> ℹ The deprecated feature was likely used in the UpSetR package. #>   Please report the issue at <https://github.com/hms-dbmi/UpSetR/issues>. #> This warning is displayed once per session. #> Call `lifecycle::last_lifecycle_warnings()` to see where this warning was #> generated.

title: Get started
text: define_profiles() builds profile strain concatenating columns binary table. Strains identical profiles put group; profile shared strain forms group single strain.
code: datafile <- system.file("data_test.csv", package = "strainselect") raw_data <- read.csv(datafile, sep = ";", header = TRUE) prepared_data <- prepare_input(raw_data, col_select = c(7, 10, 13, 14, 17, 24),                                id = 1, date = 17) #> no duplicate ID #> selected metadata: CONTEXTE, MATRICE1, REGION, SECTEUR, LIEUPVT, ANNEE upset_data <- prepare_upset(prepared_data) upset_profiles <- define_profiles(upset_data) # number of distinct profiles max(upset_profiles$group) #> [1] 61

title: Get started
text: Finally, select_profiles() selects one strain per group. group containing single strain gets strain; since strains larger group identical, one chosen random. Use seed make selection reproducible.
code: datafile <- system.file("data_test.csv", package = "strainselect") raw_data <- read.csv(datafile, sep = ";", header = TRUE) prepared_data <- prepare_input(raw_data, col_select = c(7, 10, 13, 14, 17, 24),                                id = 1, date = 17) #> no duplicate ID #> selected metadata: CONTEXTE, MATRICE1, REGION, SECTEUR, LIEUPVT, ANNEE upset_profiles <- define_profiles(prepare_upset(prepared_data)) selection <- select_profiles(upset_profiles, prepared_data, seed = 1) # one strain per distinct profile length(unique(selection$selected)) #> [1] 61

what: strainselect: Select Bacterial Strains to Sequence Based on Their Metadata — strainselect-package
title: strainselect: Select Bacterial Strains to Sequence Based on Their Metadata — strainselect-package
text: Helps choosing bacterial strains sequence collection described categorical metadata (sampling context, matrix, region, year...). Two methods provided. clustering method groups strains chosen number clusters using Gower distance hierarchical clustering, selects best clustered strain cluster according silhouette width; suited number strains can sequenced limited. profile method groups strains share exactly metadata selects one strain per group, every distinct profile represented.

title: strainselect: Select Bacterial Strains to Sequence Based on Their Metadata — strainselect-package
text: methods start prepare_input(), cleans table metadata. clustering method suited number strains can sequenced limited: assess_gower() computes Gower distances hierarchical clustering, cstats_table() helps choosing number clusters, select_silhouette() selects best clustered strain cluster. profile method suited number strains limited: prepare_upset() builds binary table modalities, define_profiles() groups strictly identical strains, select_profiles() selects one strain per group. See vignette("get-started", package = "strainselect") complete example.
